newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia investment up 10 pct in 1996 - institute.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia investment up 10 pct in 1996 - institute.

text.p: Total investment in Slovenia was estimated to have grown by 10 percent to 555 billion tolars ($3.7 billion) in 1996, the government-sponsored Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said on Monday.
"The largest rise of investment was registered in road construction and in the banking sector," Lili Figar, deputy director of the institute, told Reuters.
Road and telecommunication infrastructure received the lion's share of investment by domestic and foreign companies, she said.

According to the institute's estimates, investment in road construction rose to 55 billion tolars from 49 billion in 1995, while that in telecommunications infrastructure climbed to 19 billion tolars from 18 billion.

"We expect investment to grow by some 9.6 percent in 1997," Figar said. The institute provided no breakdown for the amount contributed by foreign investors in the former Yugoslav republic. In 1995 foreign interest accounted for some five percent of the total. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
